Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all from an entertaining series opener where South Africa Women came out on top to take the lead in this three-match series. After a day's rest, the two teams will be back on the field, where South Africa Women will be looking to seal the series, whereas India Women will aim to force a series decider. The 2nd T20I will take place on Sunday, 7th July, with the first ball to be bowled at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). As always, our build-up will begin much sooner. See you then. Cheers!

Tazmin Brits is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for her brilliant knock of 81 runs from 56 balls. She starts by saying that the conditions were tough and can't really explain what it was like. Shares that despite scoring the runs, she is not happy with herself. Feels that she was letting the team down through her struggles early on. Tells that she was experiencing cramps in her right leg but hopes to be fine for the next game. Says that she did not have a great time in the ODIs and sat out in the Test but she is happy to get the win.

The skipper of South Africa Women, Laura Wolvaardt says that it's much nicer to talk after the win. Adds that it’s special, coming after three tough weeks. Shares that they fought well in the Test and finally got the win in the first T20I. Mentions that they wanted to chase in this game but batting first turned out well as the bowlers stepped up. Ends by sharing that they came out with positive intent and it was an exciting game.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they did not play good cricket overall. and also dropped too many chances. Feels that they played too many dot balls in the middle phase. Lauds the way South Africa Women bowled. Reckons that the way her team started with the bat, they needed to keep going but could not because of the dot balls. Tells that with the ball, they need to be more aware of what the batter is trying to do and bowl according to the field.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Marizanne Kapp is up for a chat. She says that it took a bit longer than they would have liked but she is happy with the win. Mentions that spending time in the middle worked well for her. Further shares that they have been speaking to be positive in the camp but when they are in the middle, they tend to be conservative. Shares that she is close to bowling again and slowly working her way towards it. Lauds Tazmin Brits for her brilliant innings and adds that she struggled initially but the others took the mantle and that they could finish well.

Earlier in the game, after being inserted into bat, South Africa Women were off to a steady start. Laura Wolvaardt took the mantle and made the Powerplay count for the visitors. While Tazmin Brits was slow to get into the groove, Marizanne Kapp had no such problems and hit a couple of early boundaries to get going. With Brits eventually finding her feet, the duo dominated the middle phase and did not allow the Indian bowlers to settle. Both batters notched up their respective fifties and put on a 96-run stand. Kapp fell on 56 but Brits carried on her merry way to set her side up for a strong finish. However, South Africa Women could only manage 12 runs off the last two overs, resulting in them finishing with 189. For India, Pooja Vastrakar was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 2 for 23 from her 4 overs.

As for India Women, they started brilliantly in the Powerplay but could maintain that tempo in the middle phase and could never really get out of that rut. They were also not up to the mark in the field and had they taken those chances, the result would have been different for the hosts. In pursuit of 190 runs, India got off the blocks quickly. Smriti Mandhana did not miss out on punishing the loose deliveries on offer as did Shafali Verma. Shafali could not kick on and her departure combined with Mandhana not getting much of the strike, resulted in the run rate dropping. With Dayalan Hemalatha struggling to find the fence, Mandhana sensed the need to up the ante and perished in doing so. Jemimah Rodrigues and Harmanpreet Kaur were left playing catchup and took the chase deep with the former being the more fluent of the two batters. Only three times in the last 8 overs did India manage to score more than 10 in an over and it proved to be a mountain too steep to climb.

South Africa Women get over the line for the first time on this tour of India! The visitors held their nerves on the night to draw the first blood in this three-match T20I series. Having left a few runs out there with the bat, South Africa Women were on the hunt for early wickets. It did not go according to the plan for them as they were all over the place with their lines and lengths. Soon they picked themselves up and the ease in field restrictions allowed them to put the squeeze on. A double strike through Nonkululeko Mlaba and Nadine de Klerk allowed them to put India on the back foot and post that, it was just about using the conditions to their advantage. They did just that as they kept bowling into the surface and never really allowed India to hit the top gear. With 20 runs to defend in the final over, Nonkululeko Mlaba was hit for a boundary on the first ball but fought back and sealed the deal for her side.

OUT! STUMPED! South Africa Women get their first win on the tour! Mlaba bowls it full and it spins away, just outside off. Harmanpreet Kaur shimmies down to go big on the off side but misses. Sinalo Jafta fumbles on the first attempt but takes off the bails in the second. South Africa Women win by 12 runs and are off to a winning start in the three-match T20I series.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Short and way outside the tramline. Dayalan Hemalatha slashes hard but does not connect. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Annerie Dercksen to Dayalan Hemalatha, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, outside off. Dayalan Hemalatha looks to play the upper cut but does not connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Annerie Dercksen to Dayalan Hemalatha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tosses it on middle. Dayalan Hemalatha slogs it toward mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Dayalan Hemalatha, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish, turning away, around off. Dayalan Hemalatha hangs back and guides it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Dayalan Hemalatha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! BANG! Floated, full, on off. Dayalan Hemalatha shimmies down the pitch and lofts it handsomely over the mid off region for a thumping boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Dayalan Hemalatha, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, outside off. Dayalan Hemalatha steers it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Dayalan Hemalatha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tosses it full on off. Dayalan Hemalatha pushes it to extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Dayalan Hemalatha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tad short and turning away outside off. Dayalan Hemalatha cuts it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Nonkululeko Mlaba to Dayalan Hemalatha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Not a great sight as live visuals show Tazmin Brits being stretchered off. The Chennai humidity seems to have taken its toll on the right-handed batter. Nonkululeko Mlaba comes into the attack now.
Full and at the stumps. Smriti Mandhana defends it watchfully on the front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Ayabonga Khaka to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, around off. Smriti Mandhana knocks it into covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Ayabonga Khaka to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, outside off. Dayalan Hemalatha guides it to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Ayabonga Khaka to Dayalan Hemalatha, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! What a way to get off the mark! Short of a length, outside off. Dayalan Hemalatha cuts it through the backward point region and it races away to the fence in a flash.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Ayabonga Khaka to Dayalan Hemalatha, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Dayalan Hemalatha walks in at number 3.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Ayabonga Khaka draws first blood! Bowls it full, around off. Shafali Verma goes hard at it and gets an outside edge that is taken neatly by the keeper, Sinalo Jafta. India lose their first wicket after getting off to a quick start.
Commentary.Howout: c Sinalo Jafta b Ayabonga Khaka
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Ayabonga Khaka to Shafali Verma, OUT! c Sinalo Jafta b Ayabonga Khaka.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched full, around off. Shafali Verma lifts it off the cue end, toward the long off region for a couple.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Ayabonga Khaka to Shafali Verma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, what happened there? Tazmin Brits is down on the ground and seems to be suffering from cramps in her right calf. Brits gets helped off the field by the physio and one of her teammates. Ayabonga Khaka is back into the attack with a change of ends.
Lands it on a length, on off, Smriti Mandhana goes for the drive but gets an inside edge that rolls towards mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Eliz-Mari Marx to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Smriti Mandhana brings up India's 50 with a six. Marx angles it in trying to tuck the batter up for room, on a shortish length, Smriti Mandhana gets inside the line early and uses the angle to pull it over fine leg for half a dozen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Eliz-Mari Marx to Smriti Mandhana, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Banged into the deck, on middle, Shafali Verma pulls it in front of square on the leg side and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dishes out a length delivery, just outside off, Shafali Verma makes room to go through the off side but miscues it off the inner half of the bat back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely shot! Right in the slot by Marx, on off, Shafali Verma does not miss out as he confidently lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in at the stumps, on a length, on middle, Shafali Verma knocks it to mid on with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Hands on heads stuff as that was not much far away from the fielder in the deep. A cross-seam delivery, on middle and leg, on a back of a length, Smriti Mandhana picks the length early and brings out the pull. Hits it flat towards deep square leg and gets it just wide of Chloe Tryon in the deep who saw the ball sail just past her outstretched right hand for a maximum.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Bangs it on a hard length, on off, Smriti Mandhana stands tall and punches it sweetly but can't get it past cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Poor delivery and it gets the treatment! Too straight by de Klerk, on the pads, on a short of a good length, Smriti Mandhana uses the angle to her advantage and helps it over short fine leg for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Glorious! Delivers it on a length and offers width on off, Smriti Mandhana holds her shape and with a still head, launches it over mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: de Klerk persists with the plan of denying the batter room to work with. This is on a length, on the pads, Smriti Mandhana fails to clip it away and wears it on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Tries to tuck the batter up for room again but slips it down leg on a fuller length for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Smartly bowled! Mandhana makes the movement to the leg side early but Nadine de Klerk spots it. Angles it in, on a nagging length and cramps the batter up for room. The ball rolls off Mandhana's pads to backward square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Nadine de Klerk to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hurls it on a length, on off and middle, Shafali Verma swipes it off the inner half of the bat and it goes straight to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Marx bends her back and dishes out a bumper, outside off, the ball gets a bit big on Shafali Verma as she takes the short ball on. Splices the pull aerially but it lands in the vacant region well away from deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a shortish length, on off, Smriti Mandhana gets on her toes and glides it down to deep third on the bounce for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Eliz-Mari Marx to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Uma Chetry will replace Richa Ghosh in the lineup as a concussion sub. Ghosh was injured in the first innings and had gone off the field. Uma Chetry took the gloves for the latter part of the innings.
Shaping in, on a good length, on middle, Smriti Mandhana loses her shape as she swings too hard and miscues the shot to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Eliz-Mari Marx to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Aimed at the pads again, on a length, Smriti Mandhana goes for the flick but the ball brushes her pads and the keeper does well to make a diving stop to her right.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Eliz-Mari Marx to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! That swung a long way! At 115 kph from around the wicket, tailing in, down leg, on a length, Smriti Mandhana misses the tickle. The keeper flings herself to her right but fails to cut it off as it races away for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Eliz-Mari Marx to Smriti Mandhana, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Going away from the batter, on a short of a good length, Shafali Verma runs it down to deep third and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Eliz-Mari Marx gets a good away shape but slips it beyond the tramline on off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Eliz-Mari Marx to Shafali Verma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes wide of the crease does Tryon and slants it in, on a nagging length, on middle and leg, Smriti Mandhana flicks it but picks out the fielder at square leg. A brisk start for India Women.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Chloe Tryon to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Pushes it through, short and wide on off, Smriti Mandhana shapes up to latch onto the width but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Chloe Tryon to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drifting into the pads, full in length from around the wicket, Shafali Verma gets her bat out in front and turns it in front of square on the leg side for one more run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Chloe Tryon to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floats it up, a bit slower, on off, Smriti Mandhana presses forward and caresses it past cover for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Chloe Tryon to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Same shot, same result! With a square leg in place, Tryon lands it short again, on middle, Smriti Mandhana is quick to rock back and gets into the position to pull it over backward square leg for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Chloe Tryon to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Too short and punished! Tryon starts from over the wicket and serves a long hop, on middle and leg, Smriti Mandhana stays low and swivels to pull it over a leaping Laura Wolvaardt at square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Chloe Tryon to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Chloe Tryon to start from the other end.
Lands it on a back of a length, around off, Shafali Verma gets on top of the bounce nicely and punches it between cover and point for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Ayabonga Khaka to Shafali Verma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Fine effort! A bit fuller and in the channel on off, Shafali Verma leans on it and times the drive well towards cover where Laura Wolvaardt makes a good diving stop to her left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Ayabonga Khaka to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mandhana shows her cards early as she backs away. Khaka follows her on a hard length, Smriti Mandhana pulls it along the ground to deep backward square leg. Gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Ayabonga Khaka to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slips on the pads, on a short of a length, Smriti Mandhana swivels in the crease for the pull but the ball sneaks under the bat and thuds her front pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Ayabonga Khaka to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping in, on a back of a length, on middle, Shafali Verma accounts for the inward movement and punches it with a straight bat to long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Ayabonga Khaka to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shafali Verma and India Women are underway! Ayabonga Khaka starts with a short delivery from over the wicket, not short enough to trouble the batter, on off. Shafali Verma nails the pull to the right of deep mid-wicket for a boundary to get going.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Ayabonga Khaka to Shafali Verma, Four!
